promptLatex: A marksman hits the target with probability 1 half on every shot, independently. Given that he hit the target at least once in his first three shots, what is the probability that he hit it on all three?
hintLatex: Both events are easiest to compute as complements of a run of misses.
Missing all three also has probability $\frac{1}{8}$, so at least one hit has probability $\frac{7}{8}$.
solutionLatex:
The three shots are independent with hit probability $\frac{1}{2}$, so hitting all three has probability $\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{1}{8}$.

Missing all three has the same probability $\frac{1}{8}$, so hitting at least once has probability $1 - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{7}{8}$.

The conditional probability of hitting all three given at least one hit is

\frac{1/8}{7/8} = \frac{1}{7}
